grclanker v0.1.3 adds an experimental, opt-in durable mode: `grclanker durable` runs the GRC agent under Pi Durable 1.3.0, so a run that crashes or is stopped can be resumed instead of started over. Nothing changes unless you run it. The release also moves the CLI to Pi 1.3.0 and the bundles to Node.js 24.22.0, makes every export atomic, stops tools when their run is stopped, and fixes checks that could pass on incomplete evidence. The tool surface is unchanged: `grclanker tools` still reports 241 domain tools and 7 compute backend tools.

## Durable mode (experimental, opt-in)

- **Three commands.** `grclanker durable run --message <text>` starts or continues a session, `grclanker durable resume --session <id>` finishes what an earlier process left unsettled, and `grclanker durable tui` opens a session in a terminal app adapted from Pi's experimental durable app. Each session is a SQLite database under `~/.grclanker/durable/sessions/<id>/`, open in one process at a time.
- **Opt-in.** The interactive CLI, the Cursor Agent SDK project, and the Flue runtime do not use it. `run` and `resume` print `grclanker durable (experimental)` to stderr, the terminal app shows it at the top of the screen, and the `--json` report carries `"experimental": true`. Commands, output, and the session format may change between releases.
- **Resume without repeating work.** Finished tool calls keep their results, interrupted read-only tools run again, and an interrupted tool that can write is reported and never rerun. Rerunning `run` with the same `--request-id` returns a settled request's stored answer without calling the model or any tool.
- **Scope.** Only the 241 domain tools are available: no compute backends, workflow prompts, skills, or subagents. The session database keeps the whole conversation, including anything pasted into a message, so treat `~/.grclanker/durable/sessions/` like a credential store.

See the [Durable Runtime guide](https://grclanker.com/docs/getting-started/durable-runtime/).

## Exports and stopped runs

- **Atomic exports.** Every `*_export_*` tool, `gws_ops_collect_evidence_bundle`, and the FedRAMP ADS bundle and site generators build in a hidden staging directory and move the finished bundle into place. An export that fails, is killed, or is stopped no longer leaves a half-written bundle. Output paths, names, rerun suffixes, and contents are unchanged.
- **Stopped runs stop their tools.** Every domain tool honors the abort signal its runtime passes. Stopping a durable command or closing the terminal app cancels in-flight API requests, ends retry waits, kills child processes such as `az`, `gcloud`, `gws`, and `trestle`, and ends collection at the interrupted read. An export stopped partway writes nothing. Runs that are not stopped behave and write exactly as before.

## Fewer passes on incomplete evidence

- **Cloudflare:** six checks no longer pass on evidence that only supports a review: permission groups whose names do not end in Read (CF-IAM-02), members whose MFA field is not `true` (CF-IAM-03), active tokens that were never used (CF-IAM-06), failed audit actions (CF-TRF-04), allow-mode IP access rules (CF-TRF-05), and quarantine-only Gateway policies (CF-TRF-06).
- **Zscaler:** a check that passed on a truncated ZIA inventory now warns and names the pages read versus the total (ZS-03, ZS-04, ZS-05, ZS-07, ZS-14, ZS-16, ZS-17, ZS-20, and ZS-25).
- **Vanta:** list calls fail on incomplete Auditor API pagination (a missing or repeated cursor, a 404 after the first page, or the 500-page cap) instead of returning a partial list.
- **CrowdStrike, KnowBe4, Snowflake, and Zoom:** CS-16 and CS-17 cap at warn when the user details lookup returns fewer users than were listed. A KnowBe4 list stops at a page entry that is not a JSON object and is marked partial. SNOWFLAKE-02 warns and names the policies whose allowlist is empty. ZOOM-COLLAB-01 warns when a non-empty trusted-domain list is truncated.
- **MuleSoft, PagerDuty, New Relic, and Salesforce:** a 200 response that omits its documented collection fails the read instead of counting as an empty inventory.
- **KEV:** `kevs_recent` and `kevs_check_ransomware` treat a zero or negative `limit`, and `kevs_recent` a negative `days`, as the documented default instead of reporting no matches.

## Runtimes

- **Pi 1.3.0**, up from 1.1.0, for `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and `@earendil-works/pi-ai`. Malformed final tool-call JSON now fails validation instead of running with partial fields.
- **Node.js 24.22.0 LTS** in the release bundles, up from 22.23.3. Source checkouts still need Node.js 22.19 or newer.
- **Flue 2.3.0**, up from 2.2.2, and **sandbox-runtime 0.0.79**, up from 0.0.78. In 0.0.79, deny rules apply through folder names with glob characters, and on Linux a sandboxed command's first network call is no longer sometimes refused.
- The Cursor Agent SDK project stays on `@cursor/bdk` 0.2.26 and still serves all 241 tools: 199 read-only and 42 approval-gated writers.

## Security

- **Flue redaction.** Tool errors, thrown exceptions, and the final reply are scrubbed of credentials that appeared in tool inputs, including encoded forms. A resumed `flue run --id` rebuilds that list from the stored conversation.
- **Vanta errors** redact the client id, client secret, and access token before they are shortened for display.
- **Config files.** A malformed or non-object `settings.json` or `models.json` is left on disk and reported without quoting it, and a broken `sandbox.json` fails closed instead of dropping your deny rules. `GRCLANKER_HOME` is refused when it reaches `.pi` through a symlink.
- **Paths.** OSCAL workspace names must be one path segment, FedRAMP bundle writes check the destination before creating directories, and RunPod staging refuses paths that leave the repository through a symlink or `..`.
- **Installers.** Official downloads stop when `SHA256SUMS.txt` cannot be fetched, has no entry for the archive, or does not match. Windows zip extraction rejects `..`, absolute, and drive-letter entries before it replaces an install.
- `npm audit` is unchanged from `v0.1.2`. The CLI has 2 high advisories, both GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv in `node-forge`, counted once directly and once through `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`. No patched `node-forge` exists yet. The site has none.

## Docs and site

- **Spec pages read as documents**, with headings, tables, section links, and a contents list. The raw markdown is a tab away, and 63 vendor reference links that opened error pages now point at the pages they name.
- **Search** finds body text and hyphenated IDs such as `SRG-APP-000148`, and corrects one-letter typos.
- **New guides** for FedRAMP readiness, the OSCAL workspace, the SCF crosswalk, KEV and EPSS, and the durable runtime. Every integration page has a Run it section.
- Docs and spec pages print black on white without the site's navigation, and tables too wide for the docs column stack on desktop too.

## Upgrade notes

- Rerun the installer to upgrade. Settings and runtime state under `~/.grclanker/agent` are kept.
- Source checkouts should rerun `npm --prefix cli ci`, since the CLI lockfile changed.
- Expect `warn` where `v0.1.2` reported `pass` on the incomplete evidence listed above, and a failed read where Vanta pagination is incomplete or a MuleSoft, PagerDuty, New Relic, or Salesforce listing omits its collection.
- **Durable sessions and the next pi-durable.** This release pins pi-durable 1.3.0. The next pi-durable release migrates a SQLite session to schema version 2 when it opens it, and pi-durable 1.3.0 or earlier cannot open a migrated session. Once a later grclanker release ships that version, a durable session it opens can no longer be opened by `v0.1.3`, so downgrading would strand it. If you might go back, copy `~/.grclanker/durable/sessions/` before opening your sessions with the newer release.

Full changelog: [What's New](https://grclanker.com/docs/changelog/) and [v0.1.2...v0.1.3](https://github.com/ethanolivertroy/grclanker/compare/v0.1.2...v0.1.3).
